subject: economics
title: PED Basics
welcome_lead: Measure how responsive demand is to price.
meta_desc: A-Level PED: definition, formula and interpretation.
final_note: PED above 1 means demand is sensitive; below 1 means it sticks.

concepts.def: Percent change in quantity demanded / percent change in price.
PED = 0 - quantity unchanged when price changes.
PED = infinity - any price rise drops quantity to zero.

walkthroughs.body_html: PED = (% change in quantity demanded) / (% change in price). Drop the minus sign and read the absolute value - over 1 is elastic, under 1 is inelastic.
PED is higher when more substitutes exist, the good is a luxury, takes a big share of income, and when buyers have time to adjust.
From perfectly inelastic (insulin) to perfectly elastic (commodity wheat for a single farmer). Most everyday goods sit in the inelastic to elastic range.

mcqs.q: What does price elasticity of demand measure?
options: PED measures whether a product is expensive or cheap.
A trade deficit means a country has no factories.
PED measures how flexible or stretchy a product is.
The responsiveness of quantity demanded to a change in price — the percentage change in quantity divided by the percentage change in price.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between a shift in demand and a movement along the demand curve?
options: A trade deficit means a country has no factories.
Demand always falls when supply increases.
A movement along the curve is caused by a change in price; a shift of the whole curve is caused by changes in other factors (income, tastes, substitute prices).
A change in price shifts the demand curve.

mcqs.q: Is a trade deficit necessarily bad?
options: Not necessarily — it can reflect strong domestic demand, attractive investment opportunities, or borrowing to fund growth. Context matters more than the headline figure.
PED measures whether a product is expensive or cheap.
A trade deficit always means a country is losing wealth and failing economically.
